correctness.rationale: Each coordinate is a union probability with monotonicity and strict radial concavity; its irreducible Jacobian at zero exceeds spectral radius one because the \(r\)-clique is supercritical. Positive Perron subsolution and all-ones supersolution give existence, strict subhomogeneity gives uniqueness and monotone squeezing gives global attraction. Symmetry yields the exact two-equation reduction. The subcritical and supercritical isolated root structure follows from strict concavity; expansion with quadratic coefficient \(q>0\) and forcing \(B\varepsilon\) gives linear, square-root and full critical-window laws. A standalone standard-library script verified 53 exact rational quadratic identities and 15 small-\(\varepsilon\) comparisons in three clique pairs; finite checks are not used for the asymptotic proof.

value.rationale: The motivating threshold-set inequality does not quantify cross-community infection amplitudes. The theorem gives a structural, model-specific division between linear leakage, critical square-root spillover and order-one endemicity, a complete explicit crossover \(Z(c)\), and a global selection/convergence result. Its finite-clique benchmark makes the critical phenomenon reproducible and directly relevant for network-modular infection models, beyond a parameter substitution or numerical table.
